        A big night of fights is set to go down in Abu Dhabi on Saturday. The UFC 333 card is headlined by a pair of title fights, including undefeated Movsar Evloev challenging Alexander Volkanovski for the UFC featherweight championship in the main event.Evloev holds a perfect 20-0 professional record, but he'll face the biggest test of his career in Volkanovski, who is on his second run as 145-pound champion at age 38.In the co-main event, Petr Yan and Merab Dvalishvili will clash in a rubber match for the bantamweight championship. Dvalishvili won their first meeting en route to winning the championship and a lengthy title run, but dropped the belt to Yan in their December rematch.Sign up for Paramount+ and watch UFC 333 for no additional fee -- every UFC numbered event and UFC Fight Night is included with your subscription! Plans start as low as $8.99/month or $89.99/year!
Every fight on the main card has meaningful implications for the UFC rankings. If Alexander Volkov wants the UFC heavyweight title shot he petitioned UFC President and CEO Dana White for, he'll need to make a statement against Rizvan Kuniev. That's especially true with Ciryl Gane vs. Josh Hokit and Sergei Pavlovich vs. Alex Pereira coming up at UFC 334 and UFC 335, respectively. Lone'er Kavanagh and Ramazan Temirov could be major flyweight players, but only one promising fighter will take a step forward in their division on Saturday. Lastly, Aaron Pico is running short on time to prove he's everything analysts predicted he'd be when he debuted in MMA in 2017. Nearly a decade later, after several ups and downs, Pico is a ranked bantamweight looking to fend off Losene Keita. It's now or never for Pico to make good on lofty expectations.
        
            
                Petr Yan hopes to serve as motivation after incredible career comeback story: 'Keep moving forward'
                
                    Brian Campbell                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
With so much happening on Saturday night, let's look more closely at the full fight card with the latest odds before we get to our staff predictions and picks for the main card that you can consider before hitting the sportsbooks.

CampbellBrookhouseMahjouriMormileWiseVolkanovski (c) vs. EvloevEvloev UDVolkanovski UDVolkanovski UDVolkanovski UDEvloev UDYan (c) vs. DvalishviliYan TKO4Yan SDYan UDYan UDYan UDKavanagh vs. TemirovTemirov TKO3Temirov TKO3Kavanagh UDKavanagh UDTemirov KO2Volkov vs. KunievVolkov UDVolkov UDKuniev UDVolkov TKO3Volkov TKO2Pico vs. KeitaKeita KO2Pico UDPico UDPico UDKeita KO1Records to date29-2331-2131-2125-2225-27Alexander Volkanovski vs. Movsar Evloev predictionsCampbell: Volkanovski's longevity has been remarkable to see, especially after he bounced back from stoppage losses to Islam Makhachev and Ilia Topuria to regain the featherweight title. But it must be said that both of his victories since those damaging defeats came against the all-action but technically limited Diego Lopes, whom Evloev defeated by decision in 2023. For whatever Evloev lacks as a finisher inside the Octagon, he has size, an incredible motor and a physical grappling style that has the potential to wear down the 38-year-old Volkanovski in the championship rounds. He also has a better fight IQ than what Lopes showed against Volkanovski over 10 rounds. Brookhouse: There are few fights where I will pick against Volkanovski until I've truly seen time catch up to him. Evloev has tremendous wrestling and a willingness to use that wrestling to grind out ugly wins, but Volkanovski has a well-rounded game that also features strong takedown defense. Volkanovski has been here before and he's got the kind of gritty, gutsy game that should require Evloev to do more than just wrestle. While Evloev has shown some strong skills when forced to fight on the feet, Volkanovski has brilliant timing and distance management tools that should let him edge out the fight on the cards.
Mahjouri: Volkanovski says he'll deliver such a sublime performance that fans will think he's de-aged. I'm inclined to believe him. The champion doesn't mean to disrespect his challenger. In fact, he believes Evloev is supremely talented. Volkanovski's confidence stems from the style matchup. He sharpened his grappling defense in preparation for two lightweight fights with Islam Makhachev. On the feet, it's his fight to lose. Volkanovski has a deeper, more nuanced striking arsenal and can fight without fear of being knocked out. Evloev has stopped three opponents by strikes, and none were in the UFC. Evloev is tenacious and will make Volkanovski work early. However, as the fight goes on, expect Volkanovski to break ahead and deliver exactly the performance he predicts.Petr Yan vs. Merab Dvalishvili predictionsCampbell: After Yan rebounded from a series of losses and injuries, he returned against Dvalishvili a new fighter in their December rematch. Yan took "The Machine" down five times, shut down Dvalishvili's wrestling attack and proved he could match him from the standpoint of pace and cardio. And if Yan can do the same and make their trilogy bout into a kickboxing match, it's hard not to imagine the same scenario from 10 months ago happening again. Dvalishvili was also hurt multiple times in their rematch, including on a pair of body kicks in Round 3 that likely would've finished any other opponent. If Yan can continue to widen the gap between them in terms of striking variety and potency, a stoppage isn't out of the question.Brookhouse: This feels like an impossible fight to pick. Yan fought brilliantly in the rematch, defending against takedowns and using great striking, including a huge body kick that badly hurt Dvalishvili. However, it's hard to know if that fight was a product of Yan hitting a new level -- or at least finding his way back to his old form -- or Dvalishvili seeing a wildly ambitious 2025 schedule catch up to him and impact his performance. My best guess is that Saturday's rubber match is an extremely close fight, and one Yan edges by his best moments on the feet being more eye-catching than what Dvalishvili produces.
Mahjouri: Dvalishvili earned the nickname "The Machine" because no human could keep up with him. Eventually, his pace broke everyone. What happens when someone can match that pace for 25 minutes? That's exactly what Yan did in his major upset win over Dvalishvili. Yan was always the more technical, powerful striker. By denying Dvalishvili's relentless takedowns and keeping pace, he chipped away with his strikes, most notably hurting Dvalishvili to the body. Maybe Dvalishvili pushed his body too far in attempting to make four title defenses in one year. But I'm inclined to believe Yan is uniquely equipped for this task. Dvalishvili's success depends on a physicality that Yan has proven he can match. I don't think the former champion has the offensive threats to change the outcome in this trilogy.Who wins Volkanovski vs. Evloev, and how exactly does the fight end? Visit SportsLine now to get detailed picks and analysis from the incomparable expert who is up over $21,000 on his UFC picks since May 2018, and find out.

title: Revisiting Seahawks' trades for Leonard Williams, Ernest Jones IV: Stars powered Seattle's Super Bowl D - CBS Sports
description: Williams and Jones were part of Mike Macdonald's defensive overhaul
body:
Williams and Jones were part of Mike Macdonald's defensive overhaul
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 24, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:14 am ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Mike Macdonald made no bones about building the Seahawks in his image. Yes, Pete Carroll had been in Seattle for more than a dozen years and built a powerhouse that won one Super Bowl and made another. But Macdonald wasn't going to just keep the status quo, nor was he going to try to build Ravens 2.0 out on the West Coast, even if he had experienced tremendous success as the Ravens defensive coordinator.The Seahawks' 2026 Super Bowl triumph, in Macdonald's second season, came from being bold. In Macdonald's first year, the Seahawks went 10-7 and just missed the playoffs — by all accounts, a good football team and a solid start to Macdonald's tenure. Macdonald didn't see it that way. He fired Ryan Grubb as offensive coordinator and brought in Klint Kubiak. Shortly before free agency began, the Seahawks released Tyler Lockett, and D.K. Metcalf requested a trade on the same day. Not only did the Seahawks trade Metcalf to the Steelers, but they also sent Geno Smith to the Raiders. It was going to be a new offense, one built more in line with how Macdonald envisioned that side of the ball. In came Sam Darnold, up stepped Jaxon Smith-Njigba, and on came the Super Bowl rings earlier this year.But the Seahawks' championship was more powered by a truly dominant defense — Macdonald's side of the ball — and to see how two key figures of that unit came to be, we have to go back to two trades: one made right before Macdonald arrived, another shortly after.
Ahead of the Seahawks' "Sunday Night Football" matchup with the Chiefs, we look back on how Seattle came away with absolute steals in acquiring defensive lineman Leonard Williams and linebacker Ernest Jones.The tradesOct. 30, 2023:Seahawks receive: DL Leonard WilliamsGiants receive: 2024 second-round pick (S Tyler Nubin), 2025 fifth-round pick (OL Marcus Mbow)With the Giants 2-6 in late October, they were looking to sell at the deadline. The 5-2 Seahawks were looking to buy, especially at pass rusher after Uchenna Nwosu's injury. Williams was in the final year of a three-year, $63 milion extension, and with the Giants having extended Dexter Lawrence the previous offseason, it looked unlikely they would also hand out a hefty deal to Williams, who was 30 at the time. The two teams consummated a deal, with the Giants taking on most of the remaining money on the agreement.After the season, even though Carroll had moved on and Macdonald had arrived, Williams remained a priority for Seattle. The Seahawks signed him to a three-year, $64.5 million deal as free agency began.
Oct. 23, 2024:Seahawks receive: LB Ernest JonesTitans receive: LB Jerome Baker, 2025 fourth-round pick (TE Gunnar Helm)This was the second trade in two whirlwind months for Jones. After playing an integral role for the Super Bowl-champion Rams as a rookie in 2021, he ascended to a starter in his second season and made 15 starts in his third year. But Jones and Los Angeles couldn't come to an extension after his third season, so the Rams shipped him and a sixth-round pick to the Titans for a fifth-round pick just before the start of the 2024 season.But the Titans were a mess to start the season (and all season, frankly, finishing 3-14 and earning the No. 1 pick). At 1-5, they traded DeAndre Hopkins to the Chiefs and, later that day, sent Jones to the Seahawks. After losing Jordyn Brooks and Bobby Wagner in free agency, Seattle had tried to fortify its linebacking corps with Baker and Tyrel Dodson on one-year deals, but it simply wasn't working out. The Titans got a linebacker to help finish out the season, plus a pick to build for the future in return.Seattle, it turned out, had unearthed a star for the second trade deadline in as many years.
Williams, Jones turn into All-Pro performersPlaying alongside 2024 first-round pick Byron Murphy, Williams was already making a big impact early in the 2024 season: 2.5 sacks, 12 quarterback hits through six weeks. But the Seahawks defense was pretty middling overall and downright bad in some spots, including 28th in yards per carry allowed.Macdonald was Baltimore's defensive coordinator when the Ravens acquired Roquan Smith from the Bears midseason. He knew a good linebacker could shape a defense, and while Jones wasn't Smith, Macdonald clearly saw him as an upgrade. It ended up being a huge one that impacted every aspect of the defenseSeahawks 2024 defense ranksBefore Jones tradeAfter Jones tradeEPA per play16th4thYards per rush28th13thNet yards per attempt15th7thJones was everywhere, racking up 94 tackles in just 10 games for Seattle. He had an interception, a forced fumble and half a sack. Though it wasn't quite enough for Seattle to make the playoffs, Macdonald could feel confident he had found his man in the middle. Williams registered 11 sacks, one-half sack short of his career high, and a career-high 16 tackles for loss.The Seahawks gave Jones a three-year, $33 million extension ahead of free agency. The strong defensive unit as a whole proved to be a precursor to what was to come in 2025.Macdonald doubled down on improving his defense after the 2024 offseason. The Seahawks signed DeMarcus Lawrence to bolster the edge and drafted do-it-all safety/defensive weapon Nick Emmanwori in the second round. The Murphy/Williams/Lawrence front became a wrecking crew, with Williams recording seven sacks and earning second-team All-Pro honors, the first of his career. He got an extension in the offseason and has three more sacks this year already.Jones was also a second-team All-Pro, having gone from a player two teams moved on from to a vital piece of arguably the league's most dominant unit. His five interceptions last year were tied for the most by any linebacker and one more than he had in his first four seasons combined. He has another interception and three sacks — 1.5 shy of his career high — already this year.This week, both will be key in slowing down Kenneth Walker III, their former teammate, who leads the NFL in rushing yards.How did Giants, Titans fare in trade returns?The most important thing to acknowledge in assessing how the Giants and Titans did is realizing that Williams and Jones wouldn't have had the same impact on their respective former teams. Macdonald is one of the game's brightest defensive minds, able to put his players in positions to succeed and develop talent everywhere. Speaking to "Hard Knocks" this offseason, Williams' wife even said Williams might have retired had he stayed with New York.The Giants' considerable trade return netted Nubin, who has been a solid player when healthy. He's had a few injuries so far in his career, but he had 98 tackles as a rookie and 78 tackles — plus seven for loss — last year. He looks like a potential long-term starter or contributor. Mbow played in 13 games as a rookie (three starts) and has appeared in six games (one start) this season. He's mostly a special teams contributor and a depth option on the offensive line.The Titans moved on from Baker after the 2024 season. He spent 2025 with Cleveland and is not currently on a team. Helm had some nice moments across a 44-catch rookie season, but he has just nine catches in six games this year. He looks like a low-level starter or solid No. 2 tight end.

body:
Tampa is looking to bounce back against the Brewers, and both clubs are looking for production from the bottom of their orders
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 24, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:04 am ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        After a thrilling Game 1, the Milwaukee Brewers are three wins away from their first World Series championship. The Brewers outlasted the Tampa Bay Rays at American Family Field on Friday (MIL 3, TB 2), and they did so after replay overturned the would-be game-ending double play. Tampa was given a second life, but did not capitalize. Jonny DeLuca struck out to end the game.   "My thought was it looked like a close play," Rays manager Kevin Cash said about the overturned double play. "(Video coordinator) Nick Rogers did a good job of recognizing that it was really close.  In the moment, I don't think he thought too strongly about it, but at that point why not challenge it?"   
The Brewers lead the series 1-0 and, historically, teams that win Game 1 of a best-of-seven have gone on to win the series 65% of the time. That said, the Los Angeles Dodgers got blown out in Game 1 of last year's World Series, then came back to beat the Toronto Blue Jays in seven. The Brewers have a leg up, but this series is far, far from being over.   Here now are three key questions heading into Saturday night's Game 2.       1. Can Rasmussen be the stopper in Game 2?    Rather than start ace Drew Rasmussen in Game 1, the Rays opted to push him back to Game 2 to give him extra rest because we're so deep into the calendar and his workload is so great. Truth be told though, extra rest is normal rest for Rasmussen, who made only seven of his 30 regular-season starts on normal four days' rest during the regular season, and none in the postseason.    
"We prioritized Drew getting an extra day," Cash explained Thursday. "He's had a pretty thick workload here.  We've relied on him heavily.  We know when he takes the ball, we're trying to get the full pitch allotment out of him."    Rasmussen had a terrific regular season and has been sensational in the postseason, allowing only three runs and 16 baserunners in 21 innings spanning three starts. He's struck out 23. The Rays need him to continue that in Game 2. Tampa is already down 1-0 in the series. It's hard to see them winning four of the next six games without Rasmussen being in top form.    Rays manager Kevin Cash declined to use his top relievers (Bryan Baker, Cam Booser, Tyler Wells) to chase a deficit in Game 1. All three should be ready to go in Game 2, potentially for 4-5 outs each. Cash can get aggressive with his bullpen but he would prefer not to. Tampa's best path to a win is Rasmussen being the stopper and pitching deep into Game 2.    
    2. Will either team get offense from the bottom of the lineup?    Game 1 was the first time since 2000 that no home runs were hit in Game 1 of the World Series. That isn't too surprising, seeing how the Brewers finished 29th in homers during the regular season, and the Rays finished 22nd. The two offenses are similar in that they have heavy hitters at the top of the order, and some glovemen at the bottom who must bunt and whatnot to contribute.    In Game 1, the two top of the orders did their part. Jackson Chourio, Jake Bauers, Christian Yelich, and William Contreras led the way for the Brewers. Yandy Díaz, Jonathan Aranda, Chandler Simpson, and Junior Caminero did the same for the Rays. The 1-2-3-4 hitters were great for both teams. Everyone else? Not so much:        BrewersRays1-2-3-4 hitters 				 				 				 				6 for 15 (.400), 3 RBI, 3B, BB 				 				 				 				6 for 14 (.429), 2B, BB 				 				 				 				Rest of the lineup 				 				 				 				2 for 15 (.133), 2B, 3 BB 				 				 				 				1 for 17 (.059), 2 RBI, BB 				 				 				 				No. 5 hitter Liam Hicks drove in both runs for the Rays, both with RBI groundouts. RBI groundouts are good, those are runs on the board, but Hicks had the tying run at second base both times. RBI groundouts are a last resort more than a means to an end. At some point, the Rays -- both teams, really -- need someone outside the 1-2-3-4 hitters to drive the ball and get a big hit.    Milwaukee is better set up to get bottom-of-the-order production. They ranked second in batting average (.248) and third in on-base percentage (.318) from the 7-8-9 lineup spots during the regular season. The Rays were 20th (.228) and 14th (.303), respectively. The stars must lead the way, but the team that gets the most production from the bottom of the order will win the World Series.        3. Can the Rays get their running game going?    The Rays went 2 for 4 stealing bases in Game 1, and that's a bit misleading. The two steals came as part of a double steal in the ninth inning, when Brewers closer Trevor Megill was focused on the batter. The two caught stealings came earlier in the game and the first was dumb, frankly. Victor Mesa Jr. got thrown out trying to steal third to end the fifth inning with Díaz at the plate.     The other caught stealing I can forgive. Aranda was running in a 3-2 count with the low-strikeout Simpson at the plate, but Simpson struck out, and Aranda was thrown out. Simpson struck out twice in Game 1 after striking out once previously this postseason. That was just a tough break. Mesa getting thrown out at third with Díaz at the plate though? Dumb baseball from a smart team.    "Ultimately, Victor is really competing," Cash said after Game 1. "Trying to do something to make something happen, put a little pressure on the defense, and it didn't work in our favor."    
The running game was one of our World Series X-factors and the Brewers figure to have a major advantage because Hicks is a poor thrower and Contreras has a great arm. Case in point: Contreras went 2 for 2 throwing out potential basestealers when he actually threw the ball in Game 1. He had two hits in the game and also shut down two rallies with his arm.    The Brewers stole just one base in Game 1 and that runner didn't even come around to score. They know they can run on Hicks (and backup catcher Nick Fortes), though. They can steal when they need it. Can the Rays? Contreras is a game-changer behind the plate, and without those extra 90 feet, pushing runs across could be a real challenge for the AL champs.    
"He's a very talented player on both sides of the ball," Cash said about Contreras. "We knew that coming in.  Not surprised by anything that he did, but that's not going to change our aggressive approach, certainly on the bases."

title: Revisiting Browns' 2026 NFL Draft: Did the K.C. Concepcion, Denzel Boston selections fix the offense? - CBS Sports
description: Concepcion and Boston are sparking the pass game, while Spencer Fano and Austin Barber have quickly solidified th
body:
Concepcion and Boston are sparking the pass game, while Spencer Fano and Austin Barber have quickly solidified the rebuilt offensive line
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 24, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:27 am ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Cleveland's offense had really struggled in recent years under head coach Kevin Stefanski. The quarterback play was inconsistent to bad, and a once dominant offensive line had deteriorated. As a result, the franchise elected to change leadership, leading to the hiring of head coach Todd Monken. The Browns are averaging 17.7 points per game this season; they averaged 14.8 points per game or less over the last two seasons. What has been the catalyst for that change? Well, they may have a few 2026 NFL Draft selections to thank.Did the receiver selections fix the offense? General manager Andrew Berry opened draft night knowing that the left tackle and wide receiver positions must be addressed. They had been considering both Texas A&M's K.C. Concepcion (Round 1, No. 24 overall) and Washington's Denzel Boston (Round 2, No. 39 overall) with their second selection in the first round. They did not anticipate Boston being available at No. 39 overall and saw it as an opportunity they could not pass up.   At times, quarterback Deshaun Watson has been on different pages from his rookie receivers. Concepcion has been led into some dangerous hits, and Boston has been forced to make contested catches rather than the ball being on him as he comes out of his break. 
The former's role had primarily been limited to the short and intermediate segments of the field. Among receivers with at least 15 receptions, his 6.60 air yards per target is the 10th-lowest in the league. Concepcion is elusive with the ball in his hands and has dispelled pre-draft concerns regarding drops — he has zero on the season. Accuracy and anticipation from a quarterback are incredibly important for a receiver like Concepcion because his greatest impact is felt post-catch. Watson has been off-target on 12.1% of his throws, according to TruMedia, which is worse than the average quarterback. Concepcion has been productive as a rookie, but the stat line could be even better. His potential is that of a high-level No. 2 in the league. Boston is an entirely different type of receiver. He has a big frame with a physical play style, a combination that has been thriving in the NFL recently.   While Concepcion ranks low in air yards per target, Boston is first (16.45) among receivers with at least 15 receptions. He shows nuance getting out of his breaks but also has the size and aggressiveness to play above the rim. Although he has been credited with zero drops, a few downfield attempts have gone off his fingertips. Better rhythm with Watson would lead to increased production for Boston. OT Spencer Fano off to a good startAdditionally, Cleveland drafted left tackle Spencer Fano (No. 9 overall). They were originally positioned to pick No. 6 overall, but traded down with Kansas City in exchange for third and fifth-round choices. LSU cornerback Mansoor Delane was picked by the Chiefs, then Ohio State linebacker Sonny Styles and Arizona State wide receiver Jordyn Tyson were taken before Fano. 
Fano started at left tackle for Utah, then moved to the right side when Caleb Lomu joined the fray. He has transitioned back to left tackle for the Browns with mixed results. A smart player who communicates and picks up exchanges well, Fano has good foot mobility, but undersets at times, and he got walked back a bit against the Panthers and Jaguars. Most of his issues are correctable, and he has been an above-average left tackle for the franchise thus far. TruMedia credits him with eight pressures and one sack allowed on 353 pass blocking snaps through six games. Long-term outlookWhen the team traded veteran Amari Cooper, it left the organization grasping at straws. They had already acquired Jerry Jeudy, but Jeudy was never meant to be the primary outlet. It is clear that Boston and Concepcion will be the team's top two targets moving forward, which has made Jeudy expendable at the trade deadline — a development few could have seen coming in April. 
Boston could be one of the top-15 wide receivers in the league. Concepcion has the potential to be a high-level No. 2 in the league.Berry was also tasked with replacing five offensive line starters in one offseason. The project began with the acquisition of Tytus Howard and continued with free agent signings of Zion Johnson and Elgton Jenkins. The unit, as a whole, has improved, but there is still work to be done. Looking forward, Johnson, Howard and, to a lesser degree, Jenkins have contracts that bind them to northeast Ohio through the 2027 season. Fano and rookie right guard Austin Barber are assured starting roles as well. The only question is whether the Browns will work Barber at right tackle and Howard at guard at some point, which Howard has done in the past.   
Fano is an average to good left tackle with the potential to be a franchise cornerstone and top-10 at his position. Cleveland has done an excellent job in the draft over the last two years and may be more reliable quarterback play away from seriously contending.

        As the NFL prepares for its first-ever game in France, when the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints square off at Stade de France on Sunday morning, security concerns continue to loom over the Week 7 international contest due to the ongoing protests in Paris. On Saturday, the league announced the closure of its "NFL House" in Paris as the French capital is gearing up for more demonstrations. Earlier this month, Parisians began rebelling against the rising cost of living and poor school conditions. Those protests, however, have turned violent, with stores being looted, property being burned, and continued clashes with police. The NFL officially announced the closure to fans on Saturday morning via its "One Pass" apps, and it comes a day after announcing the shutdown of its pop-up NFL shop due to "potential accessibility issues," according to the Associated Press. The fan events at "NFL House" on Saturday included "French Athletes in Football" and "From the Field to the Community." On top of this "NFL House" closure, the New Orleans Saints announced Saturday that their "Saints House" event has been postponed until Sunday. 
These are just the latest NFL-related cancellations due to the protests. On Thursday, security concerns led to the cancellation of a Steelers fan event in Bastille set for this weekend. Beyond the NFL, major museums, including the Louvre and Orsay Museum, are closed on Saturday, according to CBS News. Paris Saint-Germain's Ligue 1 matchup with Lyon was also moved from Sunday to Monday at the request of Paris police. The U.S. State Department issued a security alert this week that "Americans in Paris for the NFL game" should "exercise caution and be aware of their surroundings." 
While the NFL and French authorities will take every measure to ensure a safe environment for the game, these protests have raised questions about whether to play it in Paris. Despite that concern, the league and union officials told The Ringer on Saturday morning that the game is on as scheduled.

        On paper, Saturday's UFC 333 is one of the most competitive cards in years. From top to bottom, UFC 333 is loaded with tremendous fights between seemingly equally matched fighters.That competitiveness is on full display in the night's two championship fights, including bantamweight champion Petr Yan against former champion Merab Dvalishvili and featherweight champion Alexander Volkanovski against undefeated Movsar Evloev. In fact, there are only three betting favorites on Saturday's card who are at -250 or higher.Every fight on the main card has meaningful implications for the UFC rankings. If Alexander Volkov wants the UFC heavyweight title shot he petitioned UFC President and CEO Dana White for, he'll need to make a statement against Rizvan Kuniev. That's especially true with Ciryl Gane vs. Josh Hokit and Sergei Pavlovich vs. Alex Pereira coming up at UFC 334 and UFC 335, respectively. Sign up for Paramount+ and watch UFC 333 for no additional fee -- every UFC numbered event and UFC Fight Night is included with your subscription! Plans start as low as $8.99/month or $89.99/year!
Lone'er Kavanagh and Ramazan Temirov could be major flyweight players, but only one promising fighter will take a step forward in their division on Saturday. Lastly, Aaron Pico is running short on time to prove he's everything analysts predicted he'd be when he debuted in MMA in 2017. Nearly a decade later, after several ups and downs, Pico is a ranked bantamweight looking to fend off Losene Keita. It's now or never for Pico to make good on lofty expectations.With such an interesting card set for UFC 333, there will no doubt be plenty of interest in the event, including at sportsbooks. With that in mind, we've once again looked at all the event's main card fights to identify our best bets for each.After a rough 1-4 result for our best bets for UFC 332, we are sitting at an unimpressive 23-28 for the year. Now we look ahead to this weekend with the goal of getting back in the black, with our only rule remaining that all bets must be at odds of -250 or better. Let's take a look at this week's picks with odds via DraftKings Sportsbook.  

        
            
                Alexander Volkanovski chases featherweight history against Movsar Evloev at UFC 333
                
                    Brian Campbell                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Aaron Pico	vs.	Losene KeitaAaron Pico moneyline (-148)It feels a certainty that Pico ends his career as one of the biggest cases of an elite prospect failing to meet anything near his potential. Still, it's hard to overlook how good Pico is when his full game is clicking. Pico is a world-class wrestler in the most literal sense and his striking is sharp, with a particularly strong bodywork game. Where Pico has come up short is on the defensive end of things, often leaving himself open to massive shots from his opponents, as happened when Lerone Murphy knocked him out with a spinning back elbow in Pico's UFC debut. Keita has the kind of striking that can punish Pico's defensive lapses, but I don't believe he can hang if Pico mixes in grappling with fair regularity. I make this pick with all the confidence one can have heading into a Pico fight, which is to say less than you'd like.
Alexander Volkov	vs.	Rizvan KunievAlexander Volkov moneyline (-122)Volkov should be sitting on a seven-fight winning streak, but he was robbed by the judges against Ciryl Gane in 2024. Had Volkov gotten the deserved win, he likely would have fought Tom Aspinall for the title. Instead, the judges kicked off a series of events that led to Gane holding the belt after Aspinall was forced to vacate. All that aside, Volkov uses his length well and has a good jab that Kuniev will be forced to navigate just to get into range to do anything offensive. In close, Volkov has a strong clinch game. This is another competitive fight on paper, but Volkov is set up to get another tough win in this one.Lone'er Kavanagh	vs.	Ramazan TemirovRamazan Temirov moneyline (-112)Temirov is a fighter who loves to brawl and whip wild overhand rights. That's not a great long-term recipe for success, but it hasn't failed him in the Octagon yet. Wins over Charles Johnson and Steve Erceg in his two most recent outings have been impressive for Temirov, while Kavanagh sandwiched a great showing in his victory over Brandon Moreno between stoppage losses to Johnson and Brandon Royval. Kavanagh doesn't have the kind of game or mentality that makes him the right kind of opponent to reliably break Temirov's flow. This is likely fought purely in the stand-up, where Temirov's bombs should dictate the fight.
Petr Yan vs.	Merab DvalishviliPetr Yan via decision (+130)Was Yan's title win a result of him being the better fighter or Dvalishvili being exhausted in keeping a truly wild schedule for a champion at the time? That's the big question heading into Saturday. Dvalishvili controlled Yan in trademark fashion in the first fight, but Yan was nearly perfect in the rematch, fending off Dvalishvili's takedowns and punishing him on the feet. I don't feel like there's a way to answer the question of whether or not Dvalishvili had pushed himself too hard going into the rematch until the fighters are in the cage on Saturday. But I do have faith that Yan is an adaptable fighter who seemed to have figured out Dvalishvili's takedown approach and has the right skills to punish him on the feet. This fight is destined for the scorecards, but the odds are too long to take the over as a best bet, which leaves Yan via decision as the most interesting available option.
Alexander Volkanovski vs.	Movsar EvloevAlexander Volkanovski moneyline (-110)This is another fight where it's likely the fighters see the scorecards, but at -275 to go the distance, the odds are too long for the column. Evloev has tremendous wrestling and Volkanovski is 38, which both would usually be checks in the challenger's favor. However, Volkanovski has good takedown defense and isn't likely to be taken down and held there, and he's been somewhat ageless in a division where age usually catches up to fighters quickly. I don't think it's a good thing that Evloev has only fought once since December 2024, and while he could grind out an ugly win if his wrestling gets going, I simply think Volkanovski is too well-rounded, crafty and used to fighting at this level to pick against him.Who wins Volkanovski vs. Evloev, and how exactly does the fight end? Visit SportsLine now to get detailed picks and analysis from the incomparable expert who is up over $21,000 on his UFC picks since May 2018, and find out.
